title: Constants and enums
summary: final, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, and enums (UpperCamelCase types) nested in Main.

say.never: A **constant** is a value that never changes, so it's marked `final`. `static` puts it on the class itself, so it must be written *outside* `main`, up near the top of the file. Capital letters with underscores tell every reader "this one never changes".
say.bit: A constant is `static final`, declared outside `main`, named in capitals.

marks.label: belongs to the class, outside main

say.bit: A constant is a value that never changes. `static` makes it belong to the class, so it's declared **outside** `main`.

say.never: An **enum** is a type you invent yourself with a short, fixed list of allowed values. A `Light` can only be `GREEN` or `RED`, and nothing else. If you misspell one, Java stops you right away, so typos can't sneak in.
say.bit: An enum is your own type with a fixed list of values; misspellings don't compile.

say.never: An **enum** is a type you invent yourself with a short, fixed list of allowed values. An `Alliance` can only be `RED` or `BLUE`, and nothing else. The type is named like a class (`Alliance`, UpperCamelCase); only the values are in capitals. If you misspell one, Java stops you right away, so typos can't sneak in.
say.bit: An **enum** is a type you invent with a fixed list of values. A variable of that type can only hold one of them, so typos are impossible.

say.never: Put an enum **inside the class** that uses it, near the constants at the top. Careful with the curly braces: each `{` needs its own `}`. In this garage program, the `Light` enum sits next to the constant, above the methods.
say.bit: Declare enums inside the class that uses them, next to the constants. Match every `{` with a `}`.
